newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end higher after Reliance bonus news.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end higher after Reliance bonus news.

text.p: ** (1010 GMT)- Bombay blue chips stage smart recovery from
day's lows after news of Reliance Industries bonus meet
on June 26 bolsters market sentiment, traders say
** Shares of Reliance up 19.50 rupees, or six pct at 340.50
after bonus news, 8.93 million shares traded
** Bombay's top 30-share index ends 7.41 pts, at 4,089.91,
provisional off 4,046.49 -- intra-day low
** SBI shares steady at 340.50 rupees after firm announces
1996/97 net at 13.32 bln rupees from 8.32 bln last year
--net profit slightly lower than expectations, traders
** National exchange index closes 2.0 pts down at 1,157.80

The announcement of a surprise bonus issue meet by leading private sector firm Reliance Industries helped Bombay stocks rally from the day's lowest levels to close modestly higher on Thursday, traders said.
"It's been a while since these rumours had been floating and people had sort of given up," said Sanjay Vaid, chief dealer at Lloyds Securites. "The news has definitely changed the market sentiment."
The announcement of the bonus meet on June 26 came nearly a year after chairman Dhirubhai Ambani hinted that shareholders were likely to receive a bonus issue in the coming months.
The Reliance spokesman said the firm would meet to finalise a bonus issue of shares on June 26, the day Reliance's annual shareholders' meeting is due.
Reliance has issued two bonus share issues since it was listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on January 23, 1978.
Both times the firm gave investors three bonus shares for every five held. Early speculation in the stockmarket was that the company was likely to maintain this ratio.
"I'm surprised. I was not expecting a bonus," said an analyst at a foreign broking firm. "I didn't think they would do it. They have given very few bonus issues in the past."

"It shows the management's confidence in how they see the prospects of the company in the coming years. It also shows that Ambani wanted to keep his shareholders happy -- he has kept his promise," the analyst said.
Stock markets cheered the bonus meet announcement.
"Much had been expected from Reliance. Now, finally everything has been put in black and white," said R. Ramakrishnan,chief dealer at ASK-RAYMOND James Securities India.
Shares of India's largest commercial bank State Bank of India ended 1.0 rupee down at 339.0 after the announcement of its 1996/97 (April-March) financial results.
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
